name: Lakota peyote songs (Native American Church)
lineage: Lakota peyote-meeting songs of the Native American Church tradition: the canonical liturgical-song repertoire for the all-night peyote-sacrament ceremony shared across many North American Native nations through the post-1900 Native American Church organization. Performance: a singer using gourd-rattle and water-drum (small drum with water inside producing a distinctive pitched-glissando-able sound), in seated-circle configuration with the participants taking turns leading songs through the night. Repertoire combines Lakota-language songs with vocables-only material and (post-1920s) songs incorporating English-language Christian themes. Distinguished from broader powwow song by peyote-meeting's sacrament-specific liturgical context and the water-drum-and-gourd-rattle (vs powwow-drum) instrumental configuration.
